ideas.risks: The dual may characterize only a relaxed closure of the policy reward set, or may require taking closures that change the value. The support-function term may not have any usable posterior interpretation, and positive-part learnability may need a separate sign convention.
ideas.summary: Audit the proposed finitely additive dual for arbitrary infinite classes. Define the exact reward-vector set C in l_infty(Theta), prove convexity/boundedness for randomized policies, determine whether the minimax value equals sup over ba_1^+(Theta) by Hahn-Banach/separation, and track whether closure in the weak-* or norm topology changes the original policy value.
ideas.title: Finitely Additive Dual Audit
ideas.why_promising: This is the newest solver attempt's main new object. If correct, it gives an exact arbitrary-class value characterization, even though not a scalar tail theorem. If false, a precise failure mode will prevent another premature stop claim.

ideas.risks: The result may collapse to known product-closure facts and add little. Finitely additive priors can hide measurability pathologies, so the explorer must separate true policy gaps from artifacts of the dual space.
ideas.summary: Compare the finitely additive dual with the existing product-closure finite-subclass formula. Check whether ba priors exactly represent separation points in the product closure of C, whether the dual recovers the non-Borel label gap, and whether product-closed or payoff-measure dominated classes force the ba supremum to be approximable by ordinary finite priors.
ideas.title: ba Dual vs Product Closure
ideas.why_promising: It connects the new arbitrary-class proposal to accepted notes. This can clarify whether the dual is genuinely a true infinite-class theorem or just a restatement of the product-closure relaxation.

ideas.risks: Prior attempts failed through one-reveal saturation, independent-bit comparator collapse, and persistent quote cross-trades. A new construction may still lose the fixed-comparator advantage or violate the intended tail envelope.
ideas.summary: Design a limited-leakage or codebook lower-bound family and compute its finite-grid Psi value before translating it into prices. Start with many terminal laws whose reward curves are separated by a parameter but whose terminal observations have controlled TV/KL; quantify the tradeoff between revenue gap gamma, tail mass q, information kappa, and comparator value.
ideas.title: Limited-Leakage Tail Lower Rates
ideas.why_promising: Matching the power-tail upper bound is the biggest open rate problem. The finite-grid value formula gives a disciplined way to test lower-bound atoms before fighting persistent-quote effects.

ideas.risks: The desired comparator-specific bound may be false beyond two arms, or even false in the two-arm advantage game. A two-arm proof may not extend to dyadic market windows.
ideas.summary: Settle the two-arm delayed-advantage problem: can an algorithm ensure A_T >= -tilde O(sqrt(T)) and A_T >= S_T - tilde O(sqrt(TD)) with delay D? Explore reserve or fractional-wealth rules that preserve the proven solvency invariant while recovering after positive evidence, and also search for adversarial sequences ruling out the target.
ideas.title: Two-Arm Delayed Advantage
ideas.why_promising: A positive result would unlock the conditional tail-adaptive truncation theorem. A negative result would explain why fixed-H truncation may be inherently nonadaptive.

ideas.risks: Identifiable classes may be easy for reasons unrelated to compactness, and Borel nondominated counterexamples may be hard or pathological. Weak/Feller continuity alone is already known insufficient.
ideas.summary: Search for natural infinite-class no-gap hypotheses beyond payoff-measure domination. Formalize identifiable nondominated classes with Borel decoding and measurable grid argmax; separately try to build a Borel, nondominated, non-identifiable class where finite subclasses are easy but the full class has linear value.
ideas.title: Nondominated Infinite Classes
ideas.why_promising: The accepted no-gap theorem is powerful but domination is only sufficient. This direction could broaden the value characterization or reveal a natural obstruction beyond the current non-Borel pathology.

ideas.risks: This may produce only another sufficient condition, not a characterization. Hidden/labeled examples show any per-world value-tail profile alone is insufficient without predictability information.
ideas.summary: Develop last-exceedance value-tail calculus. Express comparator value and truncation loss using L_a = last time P_s > a, then test whether prefix-conditional, value-weighted last-exceedance tails give sharper upper bounds or clearer necessary obstructions than first-hitting beta.
ideas.title: Predictable Last-Exceedance Tails
ideas.why_promising: The identity sum_t r_t(a)=a(L_a-1)_+ is clean and may expose the exact value-weighted object hidden by first-hitting tails, while staying compatible with known counterexamples.

ideas.risks: The obstruction may be bypassed by doubling or randomized horizon mixing, and it concerns a separate anytime regime rather than the horizon-aware setting of the main theorem package.
ideas.summary: Formalize the horizon-free known-law obstruction using super-growing two-deadline deterministic sequences. Prove or refute that every single anytime policy suffers linear regret on one of two horizons, despite the horizon-aware known-law oracle achieving O(1).
ideas.title: Anytime Known-Law Boundary
ideas.why_promising: It would cleanly separate horizon-aware oracle learnability from anytime learnability, preventing overgeneralization of the known-law result.
